## 2

I don't think you need to trust space photos at all, because there's evidence you can check yourself. When a ship sails away, the hull disappears before the mast, which wouldn't happen on a flat surface. During a lunar eclipse, the Earth's shadow on the Moon is always round, whatever angle it's cast from. People in Australia see different stars from people in Europe, and it can be noon in one country while it's midnight in another. Around 240 BC, Eratosthenes measured the Earth's size using shadows in two Egyptian cities and came within a few percent of the modern figure, long before anyone could fake a photo. I'm curious what convinced you. What evidence would change your mind?

## 3

Sunlight looks white, but it's actually a mix of all the colours of the rainbow, and each colour is light with a different wavelength. Blue light has short waves and red light has long ones. As sunlight passes through the air, it hits tiny gas molecules, mostly nitrogen and oxygen. These molecules scatter short waves much more than long ones. Blue light gets scattered about five times more than red. So blue light bounces around the sky in every direction, and wherever you look, some of it reaches your eyes.

Violet has even shorter waves than blue, so you might wonder why the sky isn't purple. The sun gives off less violet than blue, some violet gets absorbed high in the atmosphere, and our eyes are less sensitive to violet. The blue wins.

You can see the same effect at sunset. The light then travels through much more air to reach you, so most of the blue gets scattered away before it arrives, and you're left with the oranges and reds.

雨是从傍晚开始下的，到了夜里也没有停。街灯在湿漉漉的柏油路上拉出一道道昏黄的光，偶尔有车驶过，轮胎碾开积水，发出长长的沙沙声。楼下的便利店还亮着，店员趴在柜台上打盹。我关了灯，坐在窗边听雨。雨点落在空调外机上，嗒嗒地响，节奏忽快忽慢。远处有人撑着伞匆匆走过，很快就消失在巷子口。空气里有泥土和青草的味道，凉凉的，让人想起很久以前的某个夏天。
